html:
The Brusilov Offensive was a Russian attack from June to September 1916 in what is now western Ukraine. Armies under General Aleksei Brusilov broke the front of Austria-Hungary in Russia's greatest victory of World War I.

The Allies had agreed to attack together in 1916. France, under pressure at Verdun, and Italy asked Russia to strike early. Brusilov did not mass his men at one point after days of shelling, which always gave warning. On 4 June he attacked along a front of several hundred kilometres, at many places at once, after a short, accurate bombardment, from trenches dug close to the enemy line. Two Austro-Hungarian armies fell apart. The Russians took the town of Lutsk and about 400,000 prisoners. Then German reserves arrived, the other Russian fronts did little, and the attack stalled in the marshes near Kovel.

Each side lost between half a million and a million and a half men; the figures are disputed. Austria-Hungary never recovered and leaned on Germany from then on. Romania joined the Allies and was quickly overrun. Russia's own losses wore out its army and fed the anger behind the Russian Revolution of 1917.
sum: The Brusilov Offensive was a Russian attack from June to September 1916 in what is now western Ukraine. Armies under General Aleksei Brusilov broke the front of Austria-Hungary in Russia's greatest victory of World War I.
